subject: english-language

moments.title: Syntactic Structures
moments.body: 1957: Chomsky's 'Syntactic Structures' published. Transformational generative grammar argues language structure is innate and rule-governed. The book launches the cognitive revolution in linguistics.
moments.takeaway: Chomsky's framework displaced behaviourist approaches to language within a decade. He remains one of the most influential intellectuals alive.

moments.title: Review of Skinner's Verbal Behavior
moments.body: 1959: Chomsky's devastating review of B.F. Skinner's 'Verbal Behavior' (1957). The review argues behaviourist conditioning cannot explain how children acquire complex language with the 'poverty of the stimulus' — sparse, error-ridden input.
moments.takeaway: The Skinner review is often credited as the moment behaviourism died (in language acquisition theory at least). The 'language acquisition device' (LAD) postulates innate language capacity.

moments.title: Universal Grammar and Principles and Parameters
moments.body: 1965: 'Aspects of the Theory of Syntax' introduces 'competence' vs 'performance'. 1981: 'Lectures on Government and Binding' introduces parameters. 1995: 'The Minimalist Program' simplifies the framework. Universal Grammar — the innate language faculty — remains controversial.
moments.takeaway: Critics of UG (Daniel Everett, Geoffrey Sampson) argue it overgeneralises; defenders argue it explains language universals and acquisition speed. The debate continues.

now.title: Chomsky's legacy
now.body: Generative grammar is one of the dominant traditions in linguistics. Cognitive linguistics (Lakoff, Langacker), construction grammar, usage-based approaches compete. Modern computational linguistics (transformer models) has reopened questions about whether innate structure is necessary or whether sufficient data and architecture suffice.
now.open_questions: Do large language models (LLMs) refute Universal Grammar? Some argue yes — they learn language from data alone. Chomskyans argue they learn statistical patterns, not language.

reflection: A single linguist reshaped modern cognitive science, philosophy of mind, and political activism (Chomsky's anti-imperialist politics is another career). His linguistic framework, even where contested, has set the agenda for generations of work.
